question.text: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 3,-4,5 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 2,-6,1 \rangle.$ Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{a} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{b} \cdot \mathbf{b}} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{a_x b_x + a_y b_y + a_z b_z}{b_x^2+b_y^2+b_z^2} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3 \cdot 2 + (-4)\cdot (-6) + 5 \cdot 1}{2^2+(-6)^2+1^2} \mathbf{b} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{35}{41} \langle 2,-6,1 \rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle \dfrac{70}{41}, -\dfrac{210}{41}, \dfrac{35}{41} \right\rangle. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $\mathbf{a}=\langle 2,-4,0 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 9,7,7 \rangle.$ Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{b}$ onto $\mathbf{a}.$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{a}}\,\mathbf{b} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{a}} \mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{a_x b_x + a_y b_y + a_z b_z}{a_x^2+a_y^2+a_z^2} \mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2 \cdot 9 + (-4) \cdot 7 + 0 \cdot 7}{2^2+(-4)^2+0^2} \mathbf{a} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{10}{20} \langle 2,-4,0 \rangle \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{2} \langle 2,-4,0 \rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle -1, 2, 0 \right\rangle. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating a Vector Projection Using Components

question.text: Let $\mathbf{a}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix} x \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$ Given that the projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
question.explanation:
Since $\mathbf{a}$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $\mathbf{b}$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular.

So, we must have \[ \mathbf{a} \perp \mathbf{b} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = 0. \]

Computing the dot product, we obtain \begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} &= a_x \cdot b_x + a_y \cdot b_y + a_z \cdot b_z \\[5pt] &= -2 \cdot x + 1 \cdot 3+ 2 \cdot 1 \\[5pt] &= -2x + 5. \end{align*}

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get \begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} &= 0 \\[5pt] -2x + 5 &= 0 \\[5pt] 2x &= 5 \\[5pt] x &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{5}{2}}. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $\mathbf{c}=\langle 3,-1,2\rangle$ and $\mathbf{d}=\langle 1,1,-1\rangle.$ Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{c}$ onto $\mathbf{d}.$
question.explanation: Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain \begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{d}}\,\mathbf{c} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{c} \cdot \mathbf{d}}{\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{d}} \mathbf{d} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{c_x d_x + c_y d_y + c_z d_z}{d_x^2+d_y^2+d_z^2} \mathbf{d} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3 \cdot 1 + (-1) \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot (-1)}{1^2+1^2+(-1)^2} \mathbf{d} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0}{3} \mathbf{d} \\[5pt] &= \left\langle \,\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0} \,\right\rangle. \end{align*}

question.text: Let $\mathbf{r}=\,\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+4\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{s}=3\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}.$ Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{r}$ onto $\mathbf{s}.$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

\begin{align*} \text{proj}_{\mathbf{s}}\,\mathbf{r} &= \dfrac{\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{s}}{\mathbf{s} \cdot \mathbf{s}} \mathbf{s} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{r_x s_x + r_y s_y + r_z s_z}{s_x^2+s_y^2+s_z^2} \mathbf{s} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{(1) \cdot 3 + (3) \cdot (-1) + (4) \cdot 0}{3^2+(-1)^2+0^2} \mathbf{s} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0}{3^2+(-1)^2+0^2} \mathbf{s} \\[5pt] &= \left\langle \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0} \right\rangle. \end{align*}
